about.title: About ShrinkIt
about.description: What is ShrinkIt? A free, private image resizer by Dusrel — resize, compress and convert images on your device. No sign-up, no uploads, no watermarks.
about.intro: ShrinkIt is a free image resizer, compressor and converter created by Dusrel. It runs entirely on your own device — as a website, an Android app, a Windows app and a Chrome extension — so the images you process are never uploaded to a server. There is no sign-up, no watermark and no premium tier: every feature, including batch processing, is free for everyone.
about.s1_body: ShrinkIt resizes images by pixels, percentage, centimetres or inches, with the aspect ratio locked or free, and with stretch, crop and fit modes. It compresses images to a quality you choose — or to an exact file size, with dedicated tools that target 50 KB or 20 KB for exam forms and official portals. It converts between JPG, PNG, GIF and WebP, and it can open JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, AVIF and iPhone HEIC/HEIF files. A passport photo maker, a social media resizer with platform presets, a before-and-after comparison tool and batch processing with a single ZIP download complete the set. Every output is stripped of all metadata — EXIF, GPS location and camera details — before it reaches your downloads.
about.s2_body: ShrinkIt is built as a client-side application. When you open the website, the program is delivered to your browser once, and from that moment all the work happens locally: your image is decoded, resized, compressed and encoded in your browser's memory, using standard web technology and background workers, and the result is handed back to you as a download. The Android app, the Windows app and the Chrome extension follow the same principle on the device itself. Because there is no upload step, there is no server that receives, stores or even sees your images — and when you close the page, the images held in memory are gone with it.
about.s3_title: Private by design, not by promise
about.s3_body: Most online image tools are built around your files or your data. ShrinkIt was designed so that there is nothing to build on: no accounts, no uploads, no image storage, and outputs with all metadata removed. On the website, our host Cloudflare measures aggregate, cookie-free visit statistics — page views and loading speeds that identify no visitor — through its Web Analytics service, as the Privacy Policy describes in full. The Android app, the Windows app and the Chrome extension use no analytics at all. Your settings, such as theme and language, are stored only on your own device.
about.s4_body: The website works in any modern browser — on phone, tablet and computer — and can be installed as a web app. The Android app adds a local history of your processed images (file names and sizes only, never the image content), camera capture and a notification when a batch finishes. The Windows app brings the same tools to the desktop with native save dialogs, so files land exactly where you choose. The Chrome extension adds a ShrinkIt option to the right-click menu on any image on the web, opening it in the editor without downloading it first. Whichever version you use, the rule is the same: your images stay on your device.
about.s5_body: ShrinkIt is made for anyone who has ever been stopped by a file-size limit or a dimension requirement: students and job applicants uploading photographs and signatures to exam and recruitment portals; applicants preparing passport and visa photographs; sellers and creators preparing images for marketplaces and social platforms; and anyone who needs a smaller image for an email, a form or a website — without handing their photos to a stranger's server.
about.s6_body: Honesty about limits matters more than a long feature list. ShrinkIt does not store or back up your images, so download your results before closing the page. It does not offer HEIC as an output format, though it opens HEIC files happily. Its size presets are templates, not guarantees: whether an exam portal, an embassy or a platform accepts an output is that organisation's decision, so always check its current requirements. And ShrinkIt cannot recover a file you closed without saving — by design, there is no copy of it anywhere else.
about.s7_body: ShrinkIt is a Dusrel product, designed and maintained by Dusrel as part of a family of free, privacy-first tools. Dusrel builds software around a simple rule: a tool should do its job on the user's own device, ask for nothing it does not need, and leave the user's files exactly where they belong — with the user. If you find an error on this page or anywhere in ShrinkIt, we would rather hear about it and fix it than leave it standing.
about.a1: Yes. Every tool and every feature — including batch processing, all output formats and the apps — is free. There is no premium tier, no trial period, no watermark and no sign-up. ShrinkIt is a free Dusrel product.
about.q2: Are my images uploaded to a server?
about.a2: No. All processing happens on your own device — in your browser, or in the app or extension on your device. Your images are never uploaded to ShrinkIt, never stored by us and never seen by us. You can confirm this in your browser's developer tools: while an image is processed, no network request carries it anywhere.
about.q3: Which image formats does ShrinkIt support?
about.a3: You can open JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, AVIF and HEIC/HEIF images, including photos taken on iPhones. You can save results as JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP. HEIC is supported as an input only, not as an output.
about.a4: Yes. Every file ShrinkIt produces is stripped of all metadata — EXIF data, GPS location, camera model and timestamps — so a photo you share does not carry hidden details about you or your device.
about.q5: Can ShrinkIt compress an image to exactly 50 KB or 20 KB?
about.a5: Yes. The dedicated Compress to 50 KB and Compress to 20 KB tools adjust quality and dimensions until the output is at or under the target size — the limits most exam, recruitment and application portals set for photographs and signatures. A black-and-white mode is available for signature scans.
about.q6: Is there a ShrinkIt app for my phone or computer?
about.a6: Yes. Besides the website, ShrinkIt is available as an Android app, a Windows app and a Chrome extension. Every version is free and processes images on your device, and the website itself can be installed as a web app from your browser.

guide.title: Image Guide
guide.description: Learn how image file size works, how to reduce it without losing quality, and how to pick the right format — free guides from ShrinkIt.
how.description: See how ShrinkIt works in 3 simple steps — add your images, tune dimensions and format, download instantly. 100% private, in-browser, free.
hero.title: Resize an Image
info1.p1: Every digital photo is a grid of tiny coloured dots called pixels. Your camera or phone decides how many dots fit in each row and column — a 4000×3000 photo holds 12 million of them, which is where the word “megapixel” comes from.
info1.p2: Each dot has to be stored somewhere, so more dots means more bytes. The file format matters too: JPG squeezes similar colours together to save space, while PNG keeps every dot exactly as it is — which is why the same picture can weigh 200 KB in one format and 2 MB in another.
info1.p3: When a site talks about “file size”, it simply means this storage weight, usually shown in kilobytes (KB) or megabytes (MB).
info1.title: What is an image file size?
info2.p1: There are two levers, and they do different things. Resizing changes the dot grid itself — shrinking a photo from 4000×3000 to 1900×1100 throws away roughly three quarters of the pixels, so the file gets dramatically smaller without looking any different at normal viewing sizes.
info2.p2: Compression keeps the grid but stores it more cleverly. With JPG you pick a quality level: 90% looks identical to the original for most photos, while 60% can halve the file size again with only tiny artefacts if you look very closely.
info2.p3: The practical recipe: first resize to the dimensions you actually need — about 1900×1100 is plenty for the web — then save as JPG at around 90% quality. That is exactly what this tool does in one click, and your images never leave your device while it happens.
info2.title: How can I reduce my image's file size?
privacy.intro: This page explains in plain language what happens to your images when you use ShrinkIt.
privacy.s1d: When you add an image, it is read into your browser's memory. Decoding, resizing, format conversion and the download are all performed locally on your device using standard web APIs (Canvas, Web Workers). At no point is your image transmitted to ShrinkIt or to any third party, because there is no server component to send it to.
privacy.s1t: 1. Your images never leave your device
privacy.s2d: ShrinkIt strips all metadata (EXIF) from processed images. That removes camera model, GPS coordinates, timestamps, colour profiles and any other embedded data. Downloads carry no metadata at all — the data is never sent anywhere.
privacy.s3d: This site uses no analytics, no advertising trackers and no cookies for tracking. If you install ShrinkIt as an app, its offline cache also lives only on your device.
privacy.s4d: Because everything runs locally, closing the tab ends the story: there is no account to delete and no server copy to request. If you have questions about this policy, reach out via the contact page.
privacy.s4t: 4. Nothing to delete, because nothing is stored

settings.background_tip: Used when the original image has transparency but the output format does not (e.g. PNG → JPG).
settings.format_tip: JPG is best for photos; PNG keeps transparency; WebP is the modern lightweight choice; GIF suits simple graphics.
settings.lock_tip: Keeps width and height proportional while you resize.
settings.mode_crop_tip: Trims the edges to match the target proportions, then resizes — no distortion.
settings.mode_fit_tip: Fits the whole image inside the target size, keeping proportions; the rest is filled with the background colour.
settings.mode_stretch_tip: Resizes directly to the exact dimensions, even if the proportions change.
settings.quality_tip: Lower values make smaller files but lose detail — 90 is a good balance.
settings.resolution_tip: Dots per inch — used to convert cm/inches to pixels. It is never written into output files; downloads carry no metadata.
